nodes.description: Address of the contract creator, assigned in the constructor from msg.sender and used as the authorization check in kill().
Counter of deposit events, incremented inside deposit() and read by getNumberOfDeposits().
Timestamp (now + 5 minutes) after which kill() becomes callable; read by getUnlockTime() and kill().
Constructor: sets creator = msg.sender, deposits = 0 and unlockTime = now + 5 minutes.
Payable fallback function that forwards any received ether to deposit().
Payable function that increments deposits when msg.value > 0 and returns getNumberOfDeposits().
Constant getter returning the current value of deposits.
Constant getter returning the current value of unlockTime.
Destroys the contract via selfdestruct(creator) if msg.sender == creator and now >= unlockTime.
Caller-controlled address used for creator assignment in the constructor and for the authorization check in kill().
Block timestamp (now) used to compute unlockTime in the constructor and to gate kill().
selfdestruct(creator) inside kill(): destroys the contract and forwards the balance to creator.
Unchecked integer addition deposits = deposits + 1 in deposit(), susceptible to overflow.

edges.reason: Constructor assigns the caller-controlled msg.sender to the creator state variable, defining the privileged account.
The constructor writes the creator state variable.
Timestamp value now + 5 minutes is stored into unlockTime, creating a timestamp dependency that controls kill().
The payable fallback function forwards incoming ether to deposit(), so any plain value transfer enters the deposit logic.
deposit() executes the unchecked increment operation deposits = deposits + 1.
The current value of deposits is read as an operand of the unchecked addition.
The result of the unchecked addition is written back into the deposits state variable.
getNumberOfDeposits() reads the deposits state variable and returns it.
deposit() returns the value produced by getNumberOfDeposits().
getUnlockTime() reads and returns the unlockTime state variable.
kill() compares the caller-controlled msg.sender against creator as its authorization guard.
kill() reads the creator state variable to perform the msg.sender == creator check.
kill() uses the block timestamp (now >= unlockTime) as a time-based authorization condition.
kill() reads the unlockTime state variable in its guarding condition.
kill() executes the dangerous selfdestruct operation once its authorization condition holds.
selfdestruct forwards the contract balance to the creator address held in state.
